title.value: Diagnostic Approach to Pleural Effusions [source_page: 1; source_excerpt: 'Diagnostic Approach to Pleural Effusions']

diagnostic_approaches.name: Gross inspection of pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Use visual appearance and odor to suggest etiology of pleural effusion
criteria_or_scoring: turbid/foul smelling suggests complicated parapneumonic effusion or empyema
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Inspect pleural fluid appearance and odor after thoracentesis
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Milky→chylothorax; foul smell→anaerobic infection; bloody→malignancy/PE/post-CABG; ammonia odor→urinothorax
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Initial assessment of undiagnosed pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: If the ﬂuid is milky looking, then one may consider a chylothorax

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid to serum hematocrit ratio for hemothorax
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate bloody effusion from frank hemothorax
criteria_or_scoring: Pleural fluid to serum hematocrit ratio >0.5 defines hemothorax
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Send pleural fluid and serum for hematocrit and calculate ratio
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Ratio >0.5 meets criteria for hemothorax
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Bloody pleural fluid to assess for hemothorax
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: If the pleural ﬂuid to serum hematocrit ratio exceeds 0.5, then it meets criteria for a hemothorax

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid cell count – RBC threshold
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Interpretation of elevated red blood cell count in pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Order pleural fluid cell count with differential
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Elevated RBC count prompts consideration of discussed etiologies
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Exudative effusions of unknown etiology
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: elevated red blood cell count (>100,00 per mm3) on pleural ﬂuid analysis

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid cell count – WBC threshold for empyema
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify pleural infection/empyema via high WBC count
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Order pleural fluid cell count with differential
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Vast majority of cases with WBC >10,000 per mm3 represent empyema
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected pleural infection
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: a high white blood cell count (>10,000 per mm3), the vast majority of these cases represent empyema.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid eosinophilia
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Interpret eosinophil predominance in pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Order pleural fluid cell count with differential
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >10% eosinophils may suggest drug reaction, air, or blood in pleural space
limitations: often related to prior pleural intervention
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Exudative effusions of unknown etiology
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: eosinophilia (>10%) may suggest a drug reaction, air, or blood contaminating the pleural space

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid lymphocyte predominance
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Interpret lymphocyte-predominant exudates
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Order pleural fluid cell count with differential
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >50% lymphocytes may be worrisome for malignancy, CTD, TB, PE, or post-cardiopulmonary bypass
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Exudative effusions of unknown etiology
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Lymphocyte predominant exudative effusions (>50%) may be worrisome for malignancy, connective tissue disease, tuberculosis, pulmonary emboli

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid very high lymphocyte count
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Interpret very high lymphocytosis in pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Order pleural fluid cell count with differential
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >90% lymphocytes seen most commonly with malignancy, tuberculosis, rheumatoid, and sarcoid pleurisy
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Marked lymphocytic effusions
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Very high lymphocyte counts (>90%) are seen most commonly with malignancy, tuberculosis, rheumatoid, and sarcoid pleurisy.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid neutrophilia
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify acute inflammatory processes including infection
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Order pleural fluid cell count with differential
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >50% neutrophils often attributable to pleural space infections and subdiaphragmatic pathologies
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected acute inflammatory/infectious effusions
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid neutrophilia (>50%) is often attributable to pleural space infections and subdiaphragmatic pathologies

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid glucose
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Biochemical assessment for complicated effusions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure pleural fluid glucose
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: <60 mg/dL may be seen in parapneumonic effusion/empyema, TB, malignancy, or rheumatoid pleurisy
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Routine analysis of exudative effusions
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A low pleural ﬂuid glucose (<60 mg/dL) may be seen in the context of a parapneumonic effusion or empyema

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid pH
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Biochemical assessment for complicated effusions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure pleural fluid pH
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: <7.2 concerning for parapneumonic effusion/empyema, malignancy, TB, and esophageal rupture
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Routine analysis of exudative effusions
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A pH of less than 7.2 is again concerning for parapneumonic effusion or empyema, malignancy, and tuberculosis

diagnostic_approaches.name: Light’s Criteria (thresholds)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify pleural effusions as exudate vs transudate
criteria_or_scoring: Pleural fluid to serum protein ratio >0.5
Pleural fluid to serum LDH ratio >0.6
Pleural fluid LDH >2/3 upper limit of lab normal
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure pleural and serum protein and LDH, apply criteria
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Meets any threshold indicates exudative effusion
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Initial classification of pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid to serum protein ratio >0.5 Pleural ﬂuid to serum LDH ratio >0.6 Pleural ﬂuid LDH concentration >2/3 upper limit of lab normal value

diagnostic_approaches.name: Light’s Criteria—performance
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Performance characteristics of Light’s criteria
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Specificity 70–80%; 20–30% of transudates may be misclassified as exudates
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When differentiating transudate vs exudate
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the speciﬁcity can range from 70% to 80%, which means that 20–30% of transudates can be erroneously categorized as exudates

diagnostic_approaches.name: Serum–pleural albumin gradient
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify pseudoexudates and reclassify as transudates
criteria_or_scoring: Serum albumin − pleural fluid albumin >1.2 g/dL
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure serum and pleural fluid albumin; calculate gradient
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >1.2 g/dL suggests transudate in suspected pseudoexudate
limitations: Requires serum sample near thoracentesis time
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected pseudoexudate (e.g., diuretics in heart failure)
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: albumin gradient (serum albumin minus pleural ﬂuid albumin >1.2 g/dL) may be helpful to determine whether the ﬂuid is consistent with a transudate.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Serum–pleural protein gradient
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Alternate method to identify transudates when serum albumin unavailable
criteria_or_scoring: Serum protein − pleural fluid protein >3.1 g/dL
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure serum and pleural fluid protein; calculate gradient
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >3.1 g/dL may help identify transudate
limitations: use when serum albumin not available
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected pseudoexudate without serum albumin
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: serum pleural effusion protein gradient (serum protein minus pleural ﬂuid protein >3.1 g/dL while imperfect) may help identify the transudate

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid cholesterol + LDH criteria
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Alternative to Light’s criteria for exudate identification
criteria_or_scoring: Cholesterol >40 mg/dL plus LDH >0.6× upper limit of normal
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure pleural fluid cholesterol and LDH
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: As accurate as Light’s criteria for exudate identification
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When reassessing exudative status or in pseudoexudates
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid cholesterol levels of >40 mg/dL along with LDH >0.6 times the upper limit of normal have been found to be as accurate as the Light’s criteria

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid cholesterol threshold
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Predict exudative effusions using cholesterol alone
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure pleural fluid cholesterol
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >55 mg/dL predicts exudates
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Alternative biomarker for exudate vs transudate
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: exudative effusions can be predicted when pleural ﬂuid cholesterol was >55 mg/dL (sensitivity 85–94%)

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid NT-proBNP (NTPBNP)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Consider heart failure etiology of effusion
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure pleural fluid NT-proBNP
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Helpful when considering heart failure but lacks superiority to serum NT-proBNP
limitations: Given lack of superiority to serum NTPBNP
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When considering a diagnosis of heart failure
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: given its lack of superiority to serum NTPBNP, its routine use is not recommended

diagnostic_approaches.name: Thoracic ultrasound to predict complex effusion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify complex pleural effusions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Perform thoracic ultrasound and assess for complexity
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Accurately predicts complex effusion
limitations: Anechoic effusion not predictive for transudate vs exudate
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Evaluation of pleural effusion complexity
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The use of thoracic ultrasound can accurately predict a complex pleural effusion with a positive predictive value of 90%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: DUETS score (ultrasound + radiology)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate exudates from transudates using imaging features
criteria_or_scoring: 1 point each: diaphragmatic nodularity, unilateral effusion, echogenicity, pleural thickening, septations
Score ≥2 indicates high likelihood for exudate
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assign points based on ultrasound and radiology features
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Score ≥2: PPV 98.8%, NPV 100%; 1% misclassification vs 6.9% with Light’s
limitations: Requires prospective validation for routine application
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When differentiating exudate vs transudate with imaging data
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A DUETS score of ≥2 indicated a high likelihood for exudate (PPV 98.8%, NPV 100%) with 1% misclassiﬁcation compared to 6.9% using Light’s criteria ( p <0.001).

diagnostic_approaches.name: Chest radiograph (PA and lateral) for effusion detection
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Detect small pleural effusions
criteria_or_scoring: Blunting of costophrenic angle at approximately 200 ml (PA) and 50 ml (lateral)
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain PA and lateral chest radiographs
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Blunting indicates presence of fluid above volume thresholds
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: First-line imaging for suspected pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: identify even a small quantity (approximately 200 ml on PA and 50 ml on lateral projection) as blunting of the costophrenic angle.

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT features suggesting exudative pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assist identification of exudative pleural effusions via CT
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain dedicated chest CT and evaluate pleura
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Findings assist in identifying exudative effusions
limitations: Machine learning not yet clinically relevant for transudate vs exudate
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Further evaluation after initial imaging/analysis
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: identify parietal pleural thickness or nodularity, attenuation of extrapleural fat, and presence of loculations

diagnostic_approaches.name: Triglyceride level for chylothorax
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose chylothorax
criteria_or_scoring: Pleural fluid triglyceride >110 mg/dL is diagnostic
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure triglyceride level in pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >110 mg/dL supports chylothorax; explore etiologies
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Milky pleural fluid or suspected chylothorax
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A level greater than 110 mg/dL is diagnostic, and possible etiologies should be explored.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid amylase
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify subdiaphragmatic or esophageal causes
criteria_or_scoring: Elevated above upper limit of normal serum value
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure pleural fluid amylase
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Elevated amylase can be seen with pancreatitis, salivary gland tumors, esophageal rupture
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When subdiaphragmatic or esophageal pathology suspected
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: an elevated (above upper limit of serum normal serum value) amylase level in the pleural ﬂuid

diagnostic_approaches.name: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) for TB pleurisy
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of tuberculous pleural effusion
criteria_or_scoring: ADA >40 U/L in lymphocyte predominant effusion
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure ADA in pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: ADA >40 U/L in lymphocyte-predominant effusion is highly suggestive (>90%) of TB
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When TB pleurisy is a consideration
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: ADA (>40 U/L) in a lymphocyte predominant effusion is highly suggestive (>90%) of a tuberculous effusion

diagnostic_approaches.name: MTB-PCR (Xpert/Xpert Ultra) on pleural samples
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose tuberculous pleural effusion and assess rifampin resistance
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Perform Xpert or Xpert Ultra PCR on pleural samples
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Helpful addition with short turnaround and integral RIF resistance testing
limitations: Prior inhouse PCR was not standardized and labor intensive
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected pleural TB, particularly with tissue/sputum sampling
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: short turnaround time and integral rifampin (RIF) resistance testing of the newer the Xpert and Xpert Ultra test make it a helpful addition

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid cytology (general yield)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose malignant pleural effusion via cytology
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Send pleural fluid for cytology
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Diagnostic yield varies by malignancy and burden
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected malignant pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Cytology is essential although the yield ranges from 34% to 72%

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid cytology (overall sensitivity)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Performance of cytology across malignancies
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Yield dependent on primary cancer type and pleural burden
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Assessing expected diagnostic yield of cytology
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: overall sensitivity of 46% (95% CI 42–58%).

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid cytology – cancer-specific yields
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Show variability of cytology yield by cancer type
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Mesothelioma 6%, hematological 40%, lung adenocarcinoma 79%, ovarian 95%
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Estimating yield by suspected primary malignancy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: yield for mesothelioma (6%) and hematological malignancies (40%) being signiﬁcantly lower than lung adenocarcinoma (79%) and ovarian cancer (95%)

diagnostic_approaches.name: Thoracic ultrasound predictors of malignant pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Predict likelihood of malignancy by ultrasound features
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Perform thoracic ultrasound; assess pleura and diaphragm
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Pooled sensitivity 80% and specificity 90% in skilled hands
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Risk stratification for malignant pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: pooled sensitivity and speciﬁcity of 80% and 90%, respectively, in the hands of a skilled operator

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT for malignancy in pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify CT features concerning for malignant pleural effusion
criteria_or_scoring: Pleural nodules or circumferential pleural thickening
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain chest CT and evaluate pleura
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Good sensitivity but poor negative predictive value
limitations: Should not be used in isolation to exclude malignancy
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Differentiating and risk stratifying suspected malignant effusion
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: pleural nodules or circumferential pleural thickening with good sensitivity but a poor negative predictive value

diagnostic_approaches.name: PET-CT for malignant vs benign pleural effusion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate benign from malignant effusions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Perform PET-CT imaging
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Pooled sensitivity 89% and 92%, respectively; limited clinical utility
limitations: not for guiding biopsies per TARGET trial
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Support diagnosis when biopsy is negative or not possible
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: pooled sensitivity of 89% and 92%, respectively, but still has limited clinical utility

diagnostic_approaches.name: Closed (blind) pleural biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Obtain pleural tissue for diagnosis when fluid analysis is nondiagnostic
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Local anesthesia; pass Abrams/Cope needle to excise parietal pleura
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Highest yield for TB; lower for malignancy and others
limitations: declining use in favor of image guidance
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Undiagnosed effusions after fluid analysis and imaging
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Its greatest yield is for TB and is in the range of 70–80%... the yield for malignancy... much lower, less than 45%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Ultrasound-guided pleural biopsy (retrospective studies)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Image-guided pleural tissue sampling
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Real-time ultrasound guidance with cutting/Abrams/Cope needle
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Diagnostic yield 88–97%
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When pleural involvement is accessible by ultrasound
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Two large retrospective studies reported a diagnostic yield of 88–97% for ultrasound-guided biopsies

diagnostic_approaches.name: Ultrasound-guided pleural biopsy (meta-analysis)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Summarize performance and safety of ultrasound-guided biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Ultrasound-guided cutting needle biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Diagnostic yield 84%; complication rate 3%
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When considering image-guided pleural biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: diagnostic yield of 84% with ultrasound-guided biopsies... with a complication rate of 3%

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT-guided pleural biopsy (meta-analysis)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Summarize performance and safety of CT-guided biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: CT-guided cutting needle biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Diagnostic yield 93%; complication rate 7%
limitations: Higher complication rate than ultrasound-guided in meta-analysis
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When pleural targets are better visualized on CT
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: compared to 93% for CT-guided biopsies with a complication rate of 3% and 7%, respectively.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Thoracoscopy (medical thoracoscopy/pleuroscopy)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Direct visualization and biopsy of pleura for diagnosis
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Pass a camera through a port into pleural space; inspect and biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Allows thorough inspection and targeted biopsy under direct visualization
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Undiagnosed exudative effusions after prior testing
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Medical thoracoscopy or pleuroscopy is a minimally invasive procedure by which a camera is passed through a port into the pleural space.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Gram stain and culture of pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify organisms in pleural space infection
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Perform Gram stain and culture on pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: May lead to identification of a microbe
limitations: ZN stain for TB is poor
consider ADA or biopsy if high suspicion
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected pleural space infection
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Gram stain and culture should be performed and may lead to the identiﬁcation of a microbe

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid volume for cytology cell block
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Optimize cytology cell block preparation
criteria_or_scoring: Submit at least 50 ml of pleural fluid
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Collect and submit ≥50 ml for cytology
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Adequacy for cell block optimized with ≥50 ml
limitations: Impact on NGS adequacy yet to be determined
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When sending pleural fluid for cytology
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: at least 50 ml of pleural ﬂuid should be submitted to optimize the cell block preparation

diagnostic_approaches.name: Thoracoscopy (direct pleural biopsy)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Gold standard for diagnosis.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Biopsy of the pleura for tuberculosis often will reveal non-caseating granulomas and acid-fast bacilli are identified on tissue culture.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: If malig- nancy is suspected or the cause of an exudative effusion remains unclear, a diagnostic pleural biopsy should be considered.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: for malignancy, the sensitivity is in the range of 93–95% [28, 29], whereas for tuberculosis, it approaches 100% [30].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pleural fluid analysis (routine tests)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: can help establish the diagnosis and underlying cause of the effusion
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Send for routine fluid analysis (cell count, pH, LDH, protein/albumin, glucose)*
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When a pleural effusion is undiagnosed, pleural fluid analysis should be the first inva- sive diagnostic test performed.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Send for routine fluid analysis (cell count, pH, LDH, protein/albumin, glucose)*

diagnostic_approaches.name: Thoracic ultrasonography
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: standard of care for both diagnosing and managing pleural effusions
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: assesses effusion size and characteristics; assists in guiding pleural interventions
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Thoracic ultrasonography has become the standard of care for both diagnosing and managing pleural effusions.

diagnostic_approaches.description: Biochemical criteria to classify pleural effusions as exudate vs transudate.

performance.notes: Highly sensitive for exudates; pseudoexudates may occur in diuresed heart failure.

diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Ascertain if diagnostic or therapeutic drainage indicated for assessing etiology or treating symptoms

diagnostic_approaches.name: Close clinical and radiographic follow-up (nonspecific pleuritis or unexplained exudative effusion)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: follow-up with potential repeat invasive interventions based on suspicion or thoracoscopic findings

diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Patients with unexplained exudative pleural effusion and those with nonspeciﬁc pleuritis on biopsy should undergo close clinical and radiographic follow-up

treatment_algorithms.title: Diagnostic algorithm for patients with undiagnosed pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Ascertain if diagnostic or therapeutic drainage indicated for assessing etiology or treating symptoms
Diagnostic +/- Therapeutic Thoracentesis
Send for routine fluid analysis (cell count, pH, LDH, protein/albumin, glucose)*
Transudate by Lights Criteria
Exudate by Lights Criteria
Treat as transudate (Consider further discordant from clinical findings)
Work up as exudate.
If clinical suspicion is for pseudoexudate, biomarkers
Clinical review, Imaging Review, Pleural fluid cytology and cultures to and r/o malignancy
Treat Underlying Etiology & Manage Effusion
Confirmed exudate
Consider Pleural Biopsy (Ultrasound guided, Image guided or using Thoracoscopy)
decision_points_and_pathways: Assess need for diagnostic vs therapeutic drainage ->Perform thoracentesis ->Send routine fluid analysis
Apply Light’s Criteria ->If Transudate ->Treat as transudate (consider further if discordant from clinical findings)
Apply Light’s Criteria ->If Exudate ->Work up as exudate; consider biomarkers if pseudoexudate suspected
Exudate pathway ->Clinical/Imaging review + Cytology/Cultures to rule out malignancy ->If confirmed exudate, consider pleural biopsy (US-guided, image-guided, or thoracoscopy)
At any point ->Treat underlying etiology and manage effusion
alternative_approaches: Pleural biopsy approaches: Ultrasound guided, Image guided, or using Thoracoscopy

nodes.label: Diagnostic ± Therapeutic Thoracentesis
nodes.criteria: Assess need for diagnostic vs therapeutic drainage

nodes.label: Routine pleural fluid analysis
nodes.criteria: cell count, pH, LDH, protein/albumin, glucose

nodes.label: Consider pseudoexudate biomarkers
nodes.criteria: Albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL or protein gradient >3.1 g/dL; consider pleural cholesterol >40–55 mg/dL

nodes.label: Exudate workup
nodes.criteria: Clinical review, imaging, cytology, Gram stain/cultures

nodes.label: Follow-up for nonspecific pleuritis
nodes.criteria: Close clinical/radiographic follow-up; repeat interventions if suspicion

edges.condition: If malignancy suspected or etiology unclear

summary: Perform thoracentesis when diagnostic/therapeutic drainage is indicated.
Send routine pleural fluid studies: cell count, pH, LDH, protein/albumin, glucose.
Apply Light’s criteria to classify as transudate or exudate.
If exudate but pseudoexudate suspected, use biomarkers: serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL; protein gradient >3.1 g/dL; pleural cholesterol >40–55 mg/dL.
For exudates, perform clinical/imaging review; order cytology, Gram stain, and cultures.
If suspicion for malignancy persists or etiology unclear, obtain pleural biopsy (ultrasound-guided, CT-guided, or thoracoscopy).
If biopsy shows nonspecific pleuritis, ensure close clinical and radiographic follow-up.

clinical_guidelines.title: Therapeutic trial of diuretics for suspected CHF-related pleural effusion
clinical_guidelines.condition: Pleural effusion with evidence of congestive heart failure
specific_recommendations: Treat heart failure as a therapeutic challenge to determine whether the effusion is responsive to diuretics.
If the effusion is refractory, consider a more extensive diagnostic workup.
decision_points_and_pathways: If evidence of congestive heart failure ->Initiate diuretics as therapeutic challenge.
If effusion improves ->Supports CHF etiology.
If refractory ->Proceed to more extensive diagnostic workup.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pleural effusion and evidence of congestive heart failure
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: it is quite appropriate to treat the heart failure as a therapeutic challenge to determine whether the effusion is responsive to diuretics.

clinical_guidelines.title: Low threshold to evaluate pleural effusions in the elderly
clinical_guidelines.condition: Elderly patients with pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Maintain a low threshold to evaluate pleural effusions in elderly patients.
decision_points_and_pathways: Elderly patient with suspected pleural effusion ->Proceed to evaluation given atypical presentations.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Elderly patients with pleural effusion symptoms or findings
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: the threshold to evaluate pleural effusions in the elderly should be low.

clinical_guidelines.title: Use of thoracic ultrasonography as standard of care
clinical_guidelines.condition: Pleural effusion: diagnosis and management
specific_recommendations: Use thoracic ultrasonography for diagnosis, characterization, and to guide pleural interventions.
decision_points_and_pathways: Suspected pleural effusion ->Thoracic ultrasonography to assess size/characteristics and guide procedures.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with suspected or known pleural effusion
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Thoracic ultrasonography has become standard of care in both diagnosis and management of pleural effusion,

clinical_guidelines.title: First invasive diagnostic test for undiagnosed pleural effusion
clinical_guidelines.condition: Undiagnosed pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Perform pleural fluid analysis as the first invasive diagnostic test.
decision_points_and_pathways: Undiagnosed pleural effusion ->Thoracentesis with pleural fluid analysis.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with an undiagnosed pleural effusion
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid analysis should be the ﬁrst invasive diagnostic test to be performed in an undiagnosed pleural effusion.

clinical_guidelines.title: Cell count and differential in exudative effusions of unknown etiology
clinical_guidelines.condition: Exudative pleural effusions of unknown etiology
specific_recommendations: Obtain pleural fluid cell count and differential.
decision_points_and_pathways: Exudative effusion of unknown cause ->Send cell count and differential.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with exudative pleural effusions of unknown etiology
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A cell count and differential should be performed in all cases of exudative effusions of unknown etiology.

clinical_guidelines.title: Send LDH and protein to apply Light’s criteria
clinical_guidelines.condition: Evaluation of exudative vs transudative pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Send pleural and serum LDH and protein to ensure the effusion meets Light’s Criteria.
decision_points_and_pathways: Pleural effusion evaluation ->Measure pleural and serum protein and LDH ->Apply Light’s criteria.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients undergoing evaluation of pleural effusion etiology
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: LDH and protein pleural and serum levels should be sent to ensure that the effusion does indeed meet Light’s Criteria for an exudative effusion

clinical_guidelines.title: Light’s criterion: Pleural fluid to serum protein ratio
clinical_guidelines.condition: Classification of exudative pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Exudate if pleural fluid to serum protein ratio >0.5.
decision_points_and_pathways: Calculate pleural/serum protein ratio ->If >0.5, classify as exudate.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pleural effusion requiring classification
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid to serum protein ratio >0.5

clinical_guidelines.title: Light’s criterion: Pleural fluid to serum LDH ratio
clinical_guidelines.condition: Classification of exudative pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Exudate if pleural fluid to serum LDH ratio >0.6.
decision_points_and_pathways: Calculate pleural/serum LDH ratio ->If >0.6, classify as exudate.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pleural effusion requiring classification
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid to serum LDH ratio >0.6

clinical_guidelines.title: Light’s criterion: Pleural fluid LDH concentration
clinical_guidelines.condition: Classification of exudative pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Exudate if pleural fluid LDH >2/3 upper limit of lab normal value.
decision_points_and_pathways: Compare pleural fluid LDH to lab ULN ->If >2/3 ULN, classify as exudate.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pleural effusion requiring classification
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid LDH concentration >2/3 upper limit of lab normal value

clinical_guidelines.title: Interpretation: Low pleural fluid glucose
clinical_guidelines.condition: Evaluation of pleural effusion biochemical profile
specific_recommendations: Low pleural fluid glucose (<60 mg/dL) may be seen in parapneumonic effusion/empyema, tuberculous effusion, malignancy, or rheumatoid pleurisy.
decision_points_and_pathways: If pleural fluid glucose <60 mg/dL ->Consider parapneumonic/empyema, TB, malignancy, or rheumatoid pleurisy.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pleural effusion undergoing biochemical testing
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A low pleural ﬂuid glucose (<60 mg/dL) may be seen in the context of a parapneumonic effusion or empyema, tuberculous effusion, malignancy, or rheumatoid pleurisy.

clinical_guidelines.title: Interpretation: Low pleural fluid pH

specific_recommendations: Pleural fluid pH <7.2 is concerning for parapneumonic effusion/empyema, malignancy, tuberculosis, or esophageal rupture.
decision_points_and_pathways: If pleural fluid pH <7.2 ->Consider parapneumonic/empyema, malignancy, TB, esophageal rupture.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pleural effusion undergoing biochemical testing
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A pH of less than 7.2 is again concerning for parapneumonic effusion or empyema, malignancy, and tuberculosis in addition to esophageal rupture.

clinical_guidelines.title: Cytology in pleural effusion evaluation

specific_recommendations: Order pleural fluid cytology; it is essential though yield ranges from 34% to 72%.

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Cytology is essential although the yield ranges from 34% to 72% [1–5].

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Gram stain and culture should be performed and may lead to the identiﬁcation of a microbe in the context of a pleural space infection.

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: the recommendation is to consider either adenosine deaminase testing or pleural biopsy.

clinical_guidelines.condition: Suspected pseudoexudative pleural effusion (e.g., diuretic-treated heart failure)
specific_recommendations: Use albumin gradient (serum albumin minus pleural fluid albumin >1.2 g/dL) to determine transudate consistency.
decision_points_and_pathways: Suspect pseudoexudate ->Calculate serum–pleural albumin gradient ->If >1.2 g/dL, supports transudate.

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: the albumin gradient (serum albumin minus pleural ﬂuid albumin >1.2 g/dL) may be helpful to determine whether the ﬂuid is consistent with a transudate.

decision_points_and_pathways: Serum albumin unavailable ->Calculate serum–pleural protein gradient ->If >3.1 g/dL, supports transudate.

clinical_guidelines.title: Exudate identification: Pleural cholesterol plus LDH thresholds
clinical_guidelines.condition: Differentiating exudative vs transudative effusions
specific_recommendations: Use pleural cholesterol >40 mg/dL with LDH >0.6 times upper limit of normal as accurate as Light’s criteria.
decision_points_and_pathways: Measure pleural cholesterol and LDH ->If cholesterol >40 mg/dL and LDH >0.6× ULN ->Supports exudate.

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Pleural ﬂuid cholesterol levels of >40 mg/dL along with LDH >0.6 times the upper limit of normal have been found to be as accurate as the Light’s criteria

clinical_guidelines.title: Exudate prediction using pleural cholesterol
clinical_guidelines.condition: Differentiating exudative vs transudative effusions
specific_recommendations: Predict exudate when pleural fluid cholesterol is >55 mg/dL (sensitivity 85–94%).
decision_points_and_pathways: Measure pleural cholesterol ->If >55 mg/dL ->High likelihood of exudate.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients undergoing evaluation of pleural effusion
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: exudative effusions can be predicted when pleural ﬂuid cholesterol was >55 mg/dL (sensitivity 85–94%)

clinical_guidelines.title: Pleural NT-proBNP measurement: routine use not recommended
clinical_guidelines.condition: Evaluation for heart failure etiology of pleural effusion
specific_recommendations: Do not routinely use pleural fluid NT-proBNP given lack of superiority to serum testing.
decision_points_and_pathways: Considering heart failure ->Prefer serum NT-proBNP; avoid routine pleural NT-proBNP.

clinical_guidelines.title: DUETS score for predicting exudative effusions
clinical_guidelines.condition: Differentiation of exudates from transudates using imaging features
specific_recommendations: Assign 1 point for diaphragmatic nodularity, unilateral effusion, echogenicity, pleural thickening, and septations; score ≥2 indicates high likelihood of exudate.

clinical_guidelines.title: ADA for suspected tuberculous pleurisy

clinical_guidelines.title: Diagnostic approach to pleural effusions – summary recommendations
clinical_guidelines.condition: Pleural effusions (including undiagnosed; suspected malignancy; exudative effusions; malignant pleural effusions; nonspecific pleuritis)
specific_recommendations: When a pleural effusion is undiagnosed, pleural fluid analysis should be the first invasive diagnostic test performed.
If malignancy is suspected or the cause of an exudative effusion remains unclear, a diagnostic pleural biopsy should be considered.
Although thoracoscopy remains the gold standard for diagnosis, the use of ultrasound-guided pleural biopsies is increasing.
Medical thoracoscopy offers the advantage of both diagnosing and managing malignant pleural effusions in a single procedure when clinically indicated.
For patients with nonspecific pleuritis of unknown cause, long-term clinical and radiographic follow-up is essential.
Thoracic ultrasonography has become the standard of care for both diagnosing and managing pleural effusions.
decision_points_and_pathways: Undiagnosed pleural effusion ->Perform pleural fluid analysis as first invasive test
Suspected malignancy or unclear cause of exudative effusion ->Consider diagnostic pleural biopsy

alternative_approaches: Ultrasound-guided pleural biopsy as an alternative to thoracoscopy

points: 8 Abstract Approximately 1.5 million pleural effusions are diagnosed each year in the USA
Light’s Criteria are primarily used to categorize the effusions into exudates and transudates on biochemical grounds which can help ascertain the underly- ing etiology
Further biochemical, microbiologic, and histo- pathologic testing of the pleural ﬂuid can allow for identiﬁcation of a speciﬁc etiology
